messages:
maria: Quick sprint pulse — landing microbatch fastpath + cache-shim prefetch is our milestone for tomorrow. Owners: @kevin (kernel) + @sam (perf). Major deps: observability trace for cache misses (Jorge), and a canary plan from ops. Blockers?
kevin: PR is up -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 :eyes: Needs review on the kernel loop changes and a microbatch API tweak.
sam: I can run the canary perf once PR merges. I swung the perf harness this morning; seems promising on tail-latency.
maria: @kevin good — can you add a short changelog in the PR description about the API surface? ops needs that for the rollout doc.
kevin: done, added a short section + compatibility notes. Also left a note that old clients will get a 400 if they send legacy `batch_mode` payload.
jorge: Observability: tracing shows an increase in KV cache misses from ~7% -> ~18% under the microbatch scenario during our synthetic load. Stacktrace points to the new eviction heuristic in the shim. Short snippet from flame: `cache_shim::evict_if_needed` called thrice per request in some shards.
sam: Hmm that explains the hit. During a quick local run I saw p99 go 210ms -> 165ms with the kernel change but then spike to 340ms when eviction thrash happened. I have CSV samples, attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/sam/perf-samples-1719
maria: Ok, action items: 1) Kevin to revert aggressive eviction threshold to previous value unless we can gate it. 2) Jorge to add a metric for eviction_count and eviction_latency. 3) Sam to run a focused canary with 10% traffic after eviction metric is in place.
kevin: Agree. I pushed a short rollback of the heuristic in a followup commit (see PR #4321/2). It keeps the new fastpath but uses old eviction thresholds.
sam: Kicking off canary in us-west-2 now. Deploy bot: @deploy-bot start canary us-west-2 runtime-firecracker v2.3.4 ->
deploy-bot: Deploy started by sam — canary id cny-20260318-17, routing 10% traffic to canary. Notifying alerting channels.
sam: Canary smoke results so far (5m window): throughput stable, p50 28ms, p95 98ms, p99 172ms. Error rate 0.03%. Eviction_count metric is now visible (thanks Jorge). Current eviction_count ~ 2.1/min per shard.
jorge: Adding two dashboards: eviction_count and eviction_latency per shard + a trace sample link. I also added an alert (sev3) if eviction_latency > 50ms for >3m.
maria: Nice. @kevin after you merge the followup, please tag the rollforward doc and ping SRE for the A/B routing test. We want canary ramp to 30% by EOD if numbers hold.
kevin: I'll merge after CI finishes. One ask: @sam can you run the model-quality smoke (few sampling prompts) against canary to ensure output parity? I flagged a possible tokenizer boundary issue in one run.
sam: On it. Quick check: 50 random prompts, BLEU-ish checks + manual spot-checks. Will post results in 15m.
maria: Thanks team. If perf and quality look stable we cut the rollforward window at noon PST. Otherwise we freeze and triage. :thumbsup:
kevin: CI passed, merging now.
sam: Quality quick-check: 50/50 prompts identical or acceptable, 2 minor whitespace/token breaks with the new tokenizer edge-case, not catastrophic. Filing a small follow-up ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/R-789-tokenizer-boundary-fix.
maria: Great. Closing loop: milestone still on track for tomorrow, main risk was eviction thrash and tokenizer edge-case; both have mitigations/tickets. We'll reconvene in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10am for final sign-off. :calendar:
jorge: Added the dashboard links to the PR and roll docs. Leaving a short note about suspect shards with higher eviction_count to investigate tomorrow. :mag:
kevin: Thanks all — ping me if you see regression alarms.
deploy-bot: Canary ramp updated to 30% after health check passed.
maria: Sweet. End of thread.
